details:
Ferris is a browser-based Earth science platform that helps students and curious explorers investigate what is changing, where it is changing, how much it has changed, and how strong the evidence is.

Users can rotate a 3D Earth, drop a pin, and swipe between NASA Terra MODIS images from two dates. For quantitative analysis, Ferris uses monthly NASA POWER temperature and precipitation records from 2001 to 2025 at selected grid points near Singapore, Borneo, and Sumatra. Users can inspect annual trends, seasonal anomalies, and regression residuals. Ferris displays confidence intervals and significance estimates alongside the trends. The Climate Contradiction Atlas also tests whether two locations are changing at different rates while accounting for multiple comparisons.

The Machine Learning Lab lets users test six trained ridge regression models for temperature and rainfall. Models were fitted on data through 2020 and evaluated on 60 held-out months per model from 2021 to 2025. Users can compare model errors against simple baselines, replay a historical prediction, or enter their own values. The Digital Twin lets users explore how a regional model responds to different inputs, and Green Mirage uses a labeled synthetic example to show how vegetation greenness and fluorescence can diverge.

Ferris combines spatial exploration with statistical testing in one workflow. An image comparison can prompt a research question, and the analysis tools help users test that question and export the evidence behind their conclusions. We considered seasonality, dependence between observations, cloud cover, the limits of gridded data, and how to communicate uncertainty. Our goal is to make Earth science data easier to investigate and help learners explain what their findings support.

We built the web app with Astro, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Three.js renders the interactive globes and procedural asteroids, and Apache ECharts displays the data. Python, NumPy, and SciPy support data preparation, statistical analysis, and model training. The app runs in a standard browser, is hosted on Cloudflare, and has a public GitHub repository.
